{"concepts_used":["GC-0078","GC-0058","GC-0059","GC-0120","GC-0093","GC-0006"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~2","quote":"To be capable of distinguishing the applicant's goods, the scent needs to be something apart from the goods themselves. It should be neither a natural characteristic nor an expected characteristic of the product, but something added to identify the applicant's goods from those of others in the same market."},{"ref":"TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~1","quote":"The natural scent of a product will have no inherent adaptation to distinguish the goods."},{"ref":"TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~1","quote":"A masking scent has a functional purpose, and is not capable of distinguishing for that reason."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s33","quote":"(1) The Registrar must, after the examination, accept the application unless he or she is satisfied that: (a) the application has not been made in accordance with this Act; or (b) there are grounds under this Act for rejecting it."}],"answer":"Yes, as a statement of Manual practice about capacity to distinguish—but not as a complete statutory test for acceptance.

**Manual practice:** The scent should be separate from the goods themselves, neither natural nor expected, and added to identify the applicant’s goods from others in the same market [TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~2]. The Manual states that a product’s natural scent has no inherent adaptation to distinguish [TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~1].

Merely adding a scent is therefore not enough: it must perform the identifying function described above. In particular, an added masking scent has a functional purpose and the Manual treats it as not capable of distinguishing for that reason [TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~2; TMM/Part21/7/7/2/1~1].

**Act:** Section 33 requires acceptance after examination unless the Registrar is satisfied that the application does not comply with the Act or that there are grounds under the Act for rejection [TMA1995/s33]. The supplied legislation does not state a scent-specific ‘only if added’ rule; that wording comes from the Manual’s practice guidance, not the supplied statutory acceptance provision."}
